newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes slightly firmer in two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes slightly firmer in two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed a shade higher on Tuesday in two-way trade as early follow-through buying rode out late profit-taking, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$351.80/352.30 an ounce against New York's US$351.60/352.10 close on Monday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$350.20/70.
"The follow-through buying boosted gold to a day high of US$352.50/353.00 but profit-taking during the afternoon session depressed the price," a senior dealer at a local investment house said.
"Sentiment is mixed on the immediate trend and I think gold will stay range-bound, with downside support at US$348-350 levels and upside resistance at US$358, then $360."
Local gold ended HK$15 higher at HK$3,259 a tael.
The carryover charge per 10 taels of gold at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to zero from its previous fix at -4.00.
